name: Java Compilation and Execution
overview: Follow HelloWorld from source file to console. By the end, you'll know which tool to blame when 'hello' never shows up.

sections.title: Compile
sections.content: Run javac HelloWorld.java to turn source into bytecode. Syntax errors and type mismatches are caught here, before HelloWorld can disappoint you.

sections.title: Load and link
sections.content: Run java HelloWorld. The JVM loads the starting class, links it, and initializes it. Verification happens during linking.

images.caption: Compile first, then load, link, initialize, and invoke the entry point.

sections.title: Execute
sections.content: The JVM calls main. It can interpret bytecode and use its just-in-time compiler for frequently executed code. Runtime failures show up during this part of the journey.

codeExamples.title: Your First Java Source Code
codeExamples.description: A simple program that prints a message

keyPoints: Compile HelloWorld.java, run java HelloWorld, and explain what each command did.

references.title: Java Virtual Machine Specification - Bytecode Instructions

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between javac and java?
interviewQA.answer: javac compiles source. java launches a JVM and runs the application.

interviewQA.question: Can a program compile and still fail?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. Compilation can succeed even if the application later hits an invalid input, missing runtime dependency, or other error.
